key_insight: A critical-transitions-based seizure detector can estimate seizure onset and offset with near expert-level agreement while remaining interpretable and robust across varied seizure morphologies.
engineering_relevance: This offers a practical, explainable alternative or complement to black-box seizure detection pipelines for EEG/voltage monitoring in epilepsy research and potential clinical tools.
method: Uses critical-transitions theory to detect state changes in seizure recordings
Evaluates performance with receiver-operating-characteristic analysis against expert-labeled onset/offset times
Tunes parameters per recording session and also tests one general parameter set across sessions
evidence_signal: The method was tested on voltage recordings from epileptic rodents across multiple recording sessions, with performance compared to expert annotations using ROC analysis.
watch_item: Performance depends on parameter choice and recording session characteristics, so generalizing beyond the tested rodent datasets and seizure morphologies may require careful validation.
paper_title: Detecting seizure onset and offset times using human intelligence: A critical-transitions-based approach
